newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico PRI seen losing lower house majority - poll.
newsitem.headline: Mexico PRI seen losing lower house majority - poll.

text.p: President Ernesto Zedillo's party is likely to lose its majority in the lower house of congress for the first time ever, according to an opinion poll published Thursday by Covarrubias y Asociados.

The poll, commissioned by Voz y Voto magazine, showed Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) would garner 40.9 percent of the vote in the July 6 elections, short of what it would need for a lower house majority under Mexico's complicated electoral system.
"With the scenario of 40.9 percent the PRI would not reach an absolute majority in the Chamber of Deputies," Jorge Alcocer, director of Voz y Voto, said at a news conference.
He said that scenario was the most optimistic one to be derived from the survey, with "don't know" and "undecided" responses excluded.
Crude data from the poll, carried out from June 21-22 on a sample of 1,207 people in 27 states across the country, suggested the PRI would win 31 percent in the deputies' races.
The conservative National Action Party (PAN) would win 21.5 percent and the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) would receive 16.3 percent, the poll showed.
